Resolves #21874

Refs #21868 · Related: #21346 · [Cover PR](https://github.com/neomjs/pages/pull/162)

Move Harbor Museum’s $18,000 proposal to Negotiation. Proposal falls from $30,000 to $12,000 and Negotiation rises from $34,000 to $52,000. Each card shows its owner and value so a visitor can check the numbers. The phone layout puts the four stages in two rows.

Evidence: L3 (Chromium keyboard, physical pointer, reset and four worker-backed stage totals in five themes) → L3 required. AC-3 remains open for the gallery record and deployed launch. Emmy owns that work on [#21934](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21934#issuecomment-7080717900) after the landing-frame producer in #21908.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | Outside-CI: the opening frames below show the nine deals, their owners and the four dollar totals at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844. Document and viewport widths matched. |
| AC-2 | Hosted `SalesPipelineNL.spec.mjs` covers the desktop interactions and five phone openings. Outside CI at `345c3567838`, I replayed both desktop journeys at 1440 × 900 in Neo Light, Neo Dark, classic Light, classic Dark and Cyberpunk on an isolated Neural Link bridge. Each ran keyboard advance/reset and physical drag/reset with an asserted viewport theme. Every move transferred Harbor Museum’s $18,000 (Proposal $30,000 → $12,000, Negotiation $34,000 → $52,000). Every reset restored the four worker-backed column totals. **10/10 passed.** |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI: [Pages #162](https://github.com/neomjs/pages/pull/162) merged the two 1280 × 720 opening frames at 960 × 540 CSS pixels, DPR 4/3. At this size all four headers and nine cards fit. Both canonical image URLs returned the published JPEG bytes. The gallery record and its live launch remain with Emmy on #21934. |

## Deltas from ticket

The column summary producer in #21873 has merged. The split catalog’s Board family still requires recipes. #21908 supplies landing-frame capture so this example can keep its zero-step opening. The [steward’s opening-frame rule](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21140) puts state assertions in the browser spec.

**Look read by the design seat (the example overviews' look is mine; this is not the cross-family review). AC-1's look passes at the frames of `2b283d719e`.**

Read: the opening frame at 1440 × 900 and at 390 × 844, and the cover on neomjs/pages#162 (approved there, digest checked).

- **It says "pipeline" before anything moves.** Four stage totals are the largest text on the page, and each checks by eye against its cards: 10 + 9 + 6, 18 + 7 + 5, 25 + 9, 36.
- **The action is named and tied to its card.** One line says what to do, the primary button says it again, and Harbor Museum carries the marker. Reset is disabled at rest and has its enabler.
- **The phone frame holds:** two stages per row, no cut label, the controls above the board.
- **The cover is the frame a visitor lands on.** No staged state, as #21140 rules since today.

**One option, yours to take or leave, no second round for it:** at 1440 × 900 the lower third of the board is empty, and three, three, two and one deals is nearly flat. Two or three more deals in Discovery would draw the funnel a buyer expects from a pipeline. If you take it, the cover is re-shot once; if not, this frame ships as it is.
